title: ProRail replaces 288 lineside cameras with AI 'smart cameras' in 2026 and uses Genetec video analytics across 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to train dispatchers
summary: SpoorPro: ProRail swaps 288 lineside cameras for smart cameras in 2026, tests drones and runs Genetec video analytics on 7,000 cameras to flag trespassers to dispatchers; no results are given.
account: SpoorPro.nl reported on 2 February 2026 that ProRail, the Dutch rail infrastructure manager, is replacing 288 lineside cameras in 2026 with new 'smart' cameras and testing drones that fly autonomously and analyze images, quoting ProRail that these forms of camera surveillance help it see and prevent incidents sooner, making the track safer with fewer disruptions and delays; the article's photo caption says the AI cameras' images are monitored 24/7, and the rest of the text is behind a paywall. SpoorPro reported on 3 March 2026 that ProRail is bringing the 7,000 security cameras it manages into one Genetec platform monitored from its Smart Monitoring Room, that Genetec Mission Control filters and analyzes alerts and forwards relevant images to an operator with suggested actions, and that video analysis is used among other things to flag spoorlopers (people on the track), in which case the train dispatcher can warn drivers; the article quotes ProRail project lead Kristian Ruiter and Genetec's Bob van Keulen. No source gives a detection count, a stopped train or a trespass reduction attributable to the analytics, and the UIC trespass-detection trial the earlier verifier mentioned could not be identified. The date observed is the first article's publication date.
purpose: Camera upgrades and video analytics intended to detect incidents such as trespassers sooner so that dispatchers can warn drivers; no detection event is documented.
system: ProRail smart lineside cameras with Genetec Security Center / Mission Control video analytics
developer: Genetec (video management and analytics platform); the smart-camera supplier is not named
taxonomy_note: Incident detection on the railway has no Trustible type; Organizational Efficiency fits centralized monitoring and faster handling. General benefit with null depths: a deployment described in trade-press reports, one partly paywalled and one built on Genetec's statements, with no outcome attributed to the analytics.

ratings.reason: ProRail says the cameras help it see and prevent incidents sooner; no incident, detection count or delay figure is published.
Fewer trespass incidents and disruptions are the stated aim; no before-and-after data are given.

ai_role.statement: No incident is documented; the AI character of the cameras rests on SpoorPro's caption and ProRail's 'smart cameras', and the trespasser-flagging function is described by Genetec, the platform vendor. Whether the analytics changed any outcome is not reported, and the full 2 February 2026 article is paywalled.
